Demand and supply; skills and training; risk; prestige; bargaining strength; discrimination; government policy; culture.

front: Why do skilled workers earn more?
back: Training limits supply and raises productivity (and so demand), giving a higher equilibrium wage.

front: Why may private-sector pay differ from public-sector pay?
back: Private firms compete for scarce skills and pay from profit; public pay follows budget-limited scales but offers more security and pensions.

front: Why can a high-prestige job pay modestly?
back: Prestige attracts many applicants, increasing supply and holding the wage down.

front: Why may a gender pay gap remain after equal pay laws?
back: Women may be concentrated in lower-paid jobs or grades, work fewer hours, or take career breaks; the law covers only unequal pay for the same work.
